title: Unify SDK CI for semver migration and provenance-backed publishing
creator: Marco Li
description: Background: We currently have per-language CI flows that differ in version bumping, artifact layout, retry logic for publish steps, and provenance/signing practices. This causes release friction, inconsistent metadata across PyPI/npm/go modules, and makes rollbacks and audits noisy. We also want to ship a coordinated semver migration (0.x -> 1.x) so SDK consumers get a clear compatibility signal while preserving existing streaming ergonomics and retry behaviors.
description_2: Goals: 1) Unify the CI publishing pipeline across Python/TypeScript/Go so a single pipeline can produce, sign, and attest artifacts for all SDKs. 2) Implement robust retry/backoff and idempotent publish semantics for registries to tolerate transient 5xx/429 errors without human intervention. 3) Emit provenance (SLSA-compatible) and cosign attestations for every published artifact and store those alongside release metadata. 4) Update streaming SDK examples and ergonomics to match published library APIs and include sample CI test matrices for streaming integration tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- A single GitHub Actions workflow (or reusable composite actions) can produce and publish Python wheels/sdists, npm packages, and Go modules for a single PR/tag.
- All artifacts are signed with cosign and an attestation is stored in the release manifest (SLSA provenance JSON).
- Publish steps are idempotent: re-running the workflow does not create duplicate package versions or corrupt state.
- CI implements retry strategy with jitter and exponential backoff for registry calls; failures beyond threshold mark the release blocked and attach logs.
- Examples/streaming demonstrates chunked iterator usage in python, ReadableStream-friendly API for TypeScript, and context-aware stream handling in Go; these examples are executed in CI smoke tests.
- Rollout doc updated with publish and rollback steps and emergency key-rotation playbook.
implementation_notes:
High-level plan:
1) Create a reusable GH Action `redwood/sdk-publish` that accepts language param (python|ts|go), version, semver-tag, and provenance toggle.
2) Standardize versioning: adopt commitizen->changelog generation and enforce semver in CI. For migration, use a staged approach: mark 0.x -> 1.0.0 via `semver-migration` branch and provide deprecation notices.
3) Build artifacts: Python -> wheels + sdist (manylinux/macosx), TS -> bundled tgz + types, Go -> module proxy artifacts + zip.
4) Signing & provenance: run cosign to sign each artifact and generate SLSA2 provenance JSON using build metadata (builder id, git sha, build inputs). Store provenance as release assets and push attestation to our attestation GCS bucket (or GitHub OIDC server).
5) Retry/idempotency: implement a publish client library that tracks publish attempts with a server-side idempotency-key header and local state. Registry-specific notes: PyPI supports retries via twine with --non-interactive and token rotation; npm via npm-cli with --tag and checks for existing version; Go modules are tag-driven (ensure `git tag vX.Y.Z` is atomic).
6) Streaming ergonomics: update examples in `examples/streaming/` for each language to demonstrate backpressure, chunk assembly, and reconnect-safe resume. Add small harness that replays real traffic (recorded sequences) in CI.
7) Tests: add end-to-end smoke matrix that publishes to a 'staging' PyPI/npm repo (TestPyPI / GitHub Packages ephemeral) and validates signatures and provenance.
8) Rollout: canary publish to internal org repo for 48h, then push to public registries.
9) Monitoring: add dashboard panel for publish success rate, cosign failures, and attestation presence per release.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Decision: Use cosign + SLSA provenance rather than custom signing because it integrates with GitHub OIDC and external verifiers.
- Tradeoff: Building a single monolithic publish action increases coordination but reduces duplication. We accept slightly larger action complexity in exchange for consistent metadata and fewer human errors.
- Backward compatibility: We will not change public API surface in the same release as the semver major bump; the bump will be a metadata release with deprecation logs for breaking changes planned in following minor releases.
- Secrets: publish tokens will be ephemeral, scoped per repo and rotated monthly. We will add a key-rotation playbook for emergency revocation.

- [ ] Implement `redwood/sdk-publish` GH Action (python+ts+go)
- [ ] Implement idempotency client for registry operations

- [ ] Add CI smoke tests that publish to staging registries and validate signatures

- [ ] Create semver-migration branch and migration doc for consumers
- [ ] Update console docs and release playbook

rollout_plan: 1) Merge GH Action and idempotency library in feature branch. 2) Dry-run against internal staging registries, validate artifact integrity and provenance. 3) Canary: tag and publish `sdk-2026.03-canary` to internal org packages for 48 hours. 4) If metrics stable, publish to public registries during maintenance window and announce via release notes. 5) If publish failure occurs, follow rollback doc: revoke tokens, yank problematic tag, publish rollback artifact with previous tag, and notify customers.
testing:
- Unit tests for idempotency client and publish action.
- Integration tests that perform a full publish to TestPyPI / GitHub Packages staging and verify cosign signatures with public keys.
- Streaming smoke tests that run against our staging inference runtime to verify example code works with real streaming responses.
- Load check: ensure publish pipeline can handle concurrent releases without cross-mutation of artifacts.
rollback:
- Immediate actions: revoke publish tokens, disable GH Action runner queue for publish workflow.
- Revert: if corrupted artifact published, push an advisory and yanked release (PyPI yanking), and publish a patched release with corrected metadata.
- Attestation: ensure SLSA provenance is preserved for audit; store evidence in incident ticket.

- Developer guide: updating examples/streaming and semver migration notes.
